title: Real-axis least-squares bath discretization for real-time transport in quantum-dot Josephson junctions
authors: Ruixin Zhou, Bing Dong, Yiyan Wang
abstract: Efficient real-time methods are essential for resolving transient coherence and nonlinear transport in driven superconducting nanostructures. Such simulations remain challenging because finite representations of the BCS continuum generate recurrences, while the damping used to suppress them smears gap-edge structure and artificially shortens coherent lifetimes; finite-broadening regularization of the gap-edge singularity likewise imposes a lifetime-resolution floor. Here we extend the driven Liouville--von Neumann approach to superconducting reservoirs---a noninteracting quantum dot with Bogoliubov--de Gennes leads---building an explicit-Hamiltonian framework that hosts a family of bath discretizations (uniform and Gaussian baselines and a new real-axis least-squares recipe, with mode energies, spectral weights, and mode-resolved dampings optimized jointly under gap-aware constraints)---making the broadening an independently calibrated numerical parameter whose leading long-time effect extrapolates controllably along the joint ($γ\to0$, $N_b\to\infty$) refinement path while cutting computational cost by over an order of magnitude versus the high-resolution DLvN reference. The compressed baths recover established current-phase relations, multiple-Andreev-reflection structure, quasiparticle-trapping oscillations, and integer and fractional Shapiro locking; the lifetime analysis yields the parameter-free leading-order relation $κ\simeq w_{\mathrm{bath}}γ_{\mathrm{eff}}$ and resolves damping-induced decay rates below the resolution scale of a previous finite-broadening calculation. As an explicit Hamiltonian reservoir representation, the framework generalizes naturally to multiterminal normal--superconducting geometries and offers a route toward interacting impurity solvers, while finite-gap strong-drive locking amplitudes mark its present quantitative boundary.
summary: This paper presents a novel, highly efficient real-time simulation technique for quantum-dot Josephson junctions by optimizing the bath discretization using a least-squares approach. This method overcomes limitations of previous techniques by treating the numerical broadening parameter independently, leading to massive computational savings. It successfully reproduces key superconducting transport signatures while providing a robust framework for future extensions to interacting systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of developing efficient, accurate real-time simulation methods for nonlinear transport in driven superconducting nanostructures.
main_result: They introduce a novel real-axis least-squares bath discretization that significantly reduces computational cost while accurately recovering established superconducting transport phenomena.
method: The authors extend the driven Liouville-von Neumann approach by formulating the bath discretization as a constrained nonlinear least-squares optimization problem.
model_or_system: The system is a noninteracting quantum dot Josephson junction coupled to superconducting leads, modeled using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes formalism in the Nambu basis.
key_observables: Current-phase relations (CPR), multiple-Andreev-reflection (MAR) structure, quasiparticle-trapping oscillations, and Shapiro locking amplitudes.
important_parameters: The independently calibrated numerical broadening parameter ($\gamma$), the ratio $\kappa \simeq w_{	ext{bath}}\gamma_{	ext{eff}}$, and the joint refinement path $(\gamma 	o 0, N_b 	o \infty)$.
main_assumptions: The dot is treated as noninteracting ($U=0$), and the method relies on careful gauge selection (hopping-phase gauge) when implementing damping in the DLvN framework.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the system setup, the locking map on the LS-32 bath, and comparisons of static CPRs against continuum benchmarks.
paper_structure: The paper details the Hamiltonian model (Section II.A), the superconducting DLvN formulation (Section II.B), and the core least-squares bath framework (Section II.C), followed by extensive validation of observables and comparisons with other methods in Section III.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly advanced, computationally efficient numerical tool for simulating open quantum systems coupled to superconducting leads, which is central to quantum electronics and superconducting circuit QED.
